summary: Norihiko Uchida is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Yutaka Ochihara. He held an assistant post (助手) at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1962.
Norihiro Matsuura works in the fields of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. As of 2026, he is attested as a faculty member at both Otani University and the Otani Academic Society.

Norihisa Baba is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Hanazono University and the University of Tokyo under Masahiro Shimoda. He has served as professor at the University of Tokyo's Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia since 2019.
Norio Koyama is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Shinshu University and under Seitatsu Matsunami, and was attested as a professor at Taisho University in 2014.

Noritoshi Aramaki is a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He held professorships at Osaka University (~1979–1988), Kyoto University (2000), and Otani University (~2000–2006).

Noriyuki Kudo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a post-graduate student and was a lecturer at Bukkyo University, worked at IRIAB, and has served as associate professor at Soka University (attested 2000–2026).

Norman Brooke Jopson was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Cambridge and Vienna under Paul Kretschmer, Charles University, and Saint Petersburg. He served as Reader at King's College London and Professor of Comparative Philology at Cambridge (1937–1955).

Norman Cutler was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago under A. K. Ramanujan. He served as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago from around 1982 to 2002.

Norman Fischer works in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied at Colgate, Iowa, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union, as well as under Mel Weitsman and Richard Baker. He founded the Everyday Zen Foundation in 2000.

Norman Gerald Barrier was a historian and Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Duke University under Robert I. Crane. He held faculty posts at Northern Illinois University and occupied the Middlebush Chair in the Social Sciences at the University of Missouri.

Norman Mosley Penzer was an Indologist who earned an M.A. at the University of Cambridge. In 1925, he was attested as a fellow or member of several British learned societies, including the Royal Anthropological Institute and Royal Asiatic Society.
Norvin J. Hein was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Franklin Edgerton. By 1965, he was an associate professor of comparative religion at Yale Divinity School.

Nosei Fuji specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Dongguk University and served as director at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College's Buddhist Cultural Institute and as professor of Buddhist studies at Ryukoku University (attested 2011–2013).

Notto R. Thelle works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Oslo and the Norwegian Academy of Music, and held posts at the NCC Center, the University of Oslo, and Oslo Metropolitan University.

Noémie Verdon specializes in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Lausanne under Johannes Bronkhorst and Charles Genequand, where she is attested as Maître assistante in 2024.

Noël Peri was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology who studied at the Séminaire de Saint-Sulpice. He taught Western music at Tokyo University of the Arts and served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient starting in 1907.

Nyanaponika Thera was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nyanatiloka Mahathera and Mahasi Sayadaw. He founded the Buddhist Publication Society in 1958, serving as its director, editor, and president into the 1980s.

Nyingcha Duoji is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Boston University and earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, where he was supervised by Leonard van der Kuijp and taught by Mark Elliott.

Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Katok and Nyoshul monasteries and under Dudjom Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He taught numerous students, including Sogyal Rinpoche and Surya Das.
